newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's July import, export prices rise.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's July import, export prices rise.

text.p: South Korean import prices rose 5.5 percent in July from a year ago, while export prices gained 6.5 percent, both in won terms, the Bank of Korea said on Thursday.
Compared with the previous month, import prices were down 1.0 percent while export prices fell 0.6 percent, a Bank of Korea statement said.
In July, import prices for raw materials and capital goods rose by 5.7 percent and 4.3 percent respectively from a year earlier while those for consumer products climbed 3.6 percent.
Export prices of industrial goods gained 6.9 percent, and for mining products 9.6 percent. But export prices for farm, forestry and fishery products lost 2.2 percent.
A central bank official said export price of dynamic random access memory chips plunged 44.5 percent in July from a year before due to global oversupply problems.
The import prices were based on cost, insurance and freight (CIF) while export prices were free on board (FOB).
